items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: the drummer -- Irv Cotler. ... And he didn't have a bass with us, we would pick up a bass when we -- when I was with him, and myself.

ctx.x: Have you ever recorded with Frank?

No, I never recorded with Frank. I only did -- well, you know, I worked with him in Vegas quite a bit, and I did some tours with him, you know, but I just never recorded with him. Actually Al Viola was his guitarist, Al has been recording with him and working with him for years and years. But I would replace Al when Al couldn't make it or something, I would replace him. And it was quite a pleasure working with Frank because he's got that charisma, and he is quite a musician also. You know, he's just a…

You know, he carried his own key men. Of course Bill Miller, as I mentioned, was playing piano for Red Norro and Mildred Bailey when I first met him in the thirties. He's been Frank's conductor for quite a few years, and Pete Condola was the first trumpet player, and the drummer -- Irv Cotler.
